answer: A shared staking bond turns each new identity from free into costly: to join the agent economy an agent must lock collateral that is slashed if peers catch it running duplicate identities or fake attestations. One honest agent can verify a few neighbours cheaply, so a Sybil island of sock-puppets collapses the moment its members must each post a bond - the attacker pays per fake identity while honest agents pay once. Reputation then grows like a garden tended over time: a fresh identity starts at its nadir of trust and must slowly earn its way in, making mass fakery uneconomic.
